title: Jelly Roll Morton in Washington, claiming One O'Clock Jump
summary: Phillips met Morton in 1936 at a club by the Lincoln Theatre where Malachi's band rehearsed, and Morton wanted him for a band and declared they had stolen his music.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: When did you first run into Jelly Roll Morton?
No, I didn't bother with him.
Where did you run into him?
He was here. I went up where he was staying. A lady had a club, and he was supposed to have been her old man, I think. And she got tired, and he left there. He was a pain in the ass, Jelly Roll was.
He said one time he wanted to get you to join one of his bands.

Well, he said he would put a band together, and he wanted me to play with him. I told him, 'Yeah'... He couldn't get... See, John and that little band, they were rehearsing. We rehearsed up there in this place, in the club he had.
They rehearsed up there in the place where Jelly was.
What was the name of that place?
It was right up there by Lincoln Theatre on U Street upstairs. I can't think of it. It's so long now, I can't think of it.
No. Next door to the Lincoln Theatre. We just talked about it the other day.
U Street and what? What number street was it near?

Between 13th and 12th on U. On the 1300 block of U Street. There was some kind of 'N' -- I can't think of it. Anyway, that's where they used to go to rehearse. Jelly Roll was up there, and every time they'd play something, Jelly Roll would stop them. [GRANDIOSELY] 'Wait a minute! That's me. They stoled it. See, that, they stole that from me.' They were playing 'One O'Clock Jump.' [SINGS THEME] 'Ah, that's me. Right there, they stole that.' He was going crazy, you know what I mean?
